results.title: Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
Yes. ResStock’s **Geometry Wall Type data for Maine are incorrect** because of mislabeled county tax assessor source data. For example, the reported single-family detached distribution is roughly 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete/CMU. The issue report says **no fix has been implemented** and all published ResStock datasets are believed to be affected. [ResStock issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The report recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use results from nearby states, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For measures whose applicability depends on wall type**, such as wood-frame-only wall insulation: either reweight Maine results using nearby states’ wall type distributions or use nearby states’ results directly.

The investigation remains incomplete, but the team currently does not expect significant impacts on baseline energy consumption, emissions, or energy bills. Measure applicability can still be affected—for example, too few Maine dwellings may qualify for wood-frame insulation upgrades. [Impacts and recommendations](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html#impacts)
